description: Switching resolution in the options screen from 2560x1440 to 3840x2160 kills the game (Liam, 2026-10-29): the main thread's 1 MB stack overflows while the game recreates its D3D device on DXVK. Launching straight into 4K works. Find what eats the stack (game, DXVK or the NVIDIA/AMD Vulkan drivers: amdvlk32 is loaded beside the NVIDIA ICD), check vanilla d3d9 (proxy.enabled=0) and DXVK device filtering, and fix in the proxy or DXVK config. Since the J3 crash-handler fix (build 066fbd0b7c62, dev keys off) the symptom is a hang instead (Liam, 2026-10-29 11:17Z, pid 11252): the loading screen stops at about 3 %, DXVK's log ends after ResetSwapChain to 3840x2160 (a device Reset this time, no second Direct3DCreate9), the proxy log ends at the first Direct3DCreate9 with no deferred crash record, the game never recovered and Liam force-closed it through Steam at about 11:19 (a hang, not a crash), and WER LocalDumps wrote a full dump at that moment (so it should hold every thread's stack in the stuck state; check its exception record says how it was taken) (%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps\napoleon_remastered\Napoleon.exe.11252.dmp, 1.7 GB): read it first. Evidence: job/J3 proxy/runs/20261029_4kcrash (WER dumps, proxy crash-handler fix 99c4503).
title: In-game resolution change crash (stack overflow at device recreation)

description: Buttons on the `wsc jobs view` page that start a background Claude Code session for that job (Write brief on a ready needs_brief row, Implement on a ready queued row, Review on a job branch waiting for review), so it shows in `claude agents` with the job id as its name. The page is a file opened from disk and cannot start programs, so `wsc jobs view --serve` runs a small server on 127.0.0.1 with a per-run token; the page posts only (id, action), and the server checks them against the registry and the same readiness rules as `jobs next` and `jobs review`, then runs `claude --bg --name J<n>-<action> --model <row model, or the D15 default> --effort medium` in the repo root. The server writes the prompt (e.g. "Pick up job J<n>"), never the page. `jobs next` and `jobs review` take `--id J<n>` so the launched session works on that job and is refused when it is not ready. D15 as code: the server refuses a third running agent (counted with `claude agents --json`); no permission bypass. Without the server the buttons copy the command instead. Tests: unready job refused, bad token refused, the command built for each action, the agent cap.

Do: (1) classify every failed run of the last 100 as branch bug, test that cannot run locally, flaky test or workflow problem, in a committed table with run ids; (2) every push to a pull-request branch runs the whole workflow twice (push and pull_request use different concurrency refs): run once per commit; (3) find and fix the harness-windows races with workflow_dispatch -Only/-Repeat (J19's route), never by raising a timeout alone, each fix proved by a repeat run; (4) local parity: every check CI runs has a local route an agent runs before pushing (J41 covers the proxy host tests; add the wine smoke test, for example in build.sh --docker, and the harness integration cases on the PC) or a gate warning that names what was not run; (5) a red check on an open job or brief pull request does not sit unseen: the reviewer or the next session is told, without polling (D32, D34). Proof: 20 consecutive green runs of harness-windows on main with -Repeat, and the table showing each class of failure has a guard. No core/ change: a game-agnostic gate goes to warscape-core as a PR.

(2) Action fix in jobs.py (PROMPTS, LABELS, not_ready): ready when the job branch row says fix; session J<n>-fix on the row model; it addresses the latest round's findings, appends '## Fix round N' to report.md, sets status=review, pushes, never touches review.md. (3) Review readiness = branch row status review (replaces 'no review.md'). (4) jobs check: '## Round N' headings numbered, newest first, at most 3, one verdict each, row status agrees with the latest verdict. (5) wsc jobs view --serve --auto: a harness-side loop (default 5 min) reads fresh branch rows and launches every ready review and fix with no running session of the same name (no cap, D34), logging each launch; builds and briefs are not auto-started. Check whether claude agents --json lists finished sessions; only running ones may block a launch. (6) docs/REVIEW.md: round numbering, status after each verdict, the cap. Tests: fix readiness, round 2 review ready after a fix, round-3 block, check failures for a 4th round and a status/verdict mismatch, pr_policy reads the newest verdict, the auto loop launching review then fix from fixture branches.
title: Automatic review and fix rounds
